title: Low-Resource Language Eval Synthesis and Certification Handbook
author: Maya Lin
body:
Summary
-------
This handbook defines a reproducible, auditable process for synthesizing evaluation suites, certifying model readiness, and operating canary rollouts for low-resource languages (LRLs). It targets languages with limited curated datasets (estimated token-volume < 1% of en-US traffic) and covers: probe synthesis strategies, annotation contracts, evaluation metrics and thresholds, canary rollout gating, and triage playbooks for observed regressions.

Why this matters
-----------------
- LRL performance can degrade silently due to tokenization, quantization, or prompt framing differences.
- Small sample sizes amplify metric variance: we must combine synthetic probes, targeted crowdsourcing, and worst-case slicing to obtain actionable signals.
- Production regressions in LRLs are high-impact for customers in underserved regions; certification reduces false negatives and avoids shipping regressions.

Scope and applicability
-----------------------
Applies to: model onboarding, quantization migrations, prompt-template changes, and routing/policy changes that affect generation or embeddings. Excludes: non-production research experiments or internal-only prototypes.

Definitions
-----------
- LRL (Low-Resource Language): language codenamed in our catalog as having < 10k high-quality parallel prompts (see language-registry).
- Anchor prompts: small, human-curated set (20–50) per intent family used to detect semantic drift.
- Synthetic families: algorithmically generated perturbations (morphological variants, code-switching, spacing) seeded from anchors.
- Certification: a documented pass/fail outcome that authorizes rollout to production.

High-level process (one-line)
----------------------------
1) Gather language telemetry -> 2) Build anchor and synthetic probe families -> 3) Run multi-fidelity evaluations (shadow + offline) -> 4) Apply statistical gating and human review -> 5) Certify or remediate -> 6) Canary rollout with adaptive reversion.

Owners and contacts
-------------------
- Primary owner: Applied ML — Evaluation Platform (team: applied-ml-evals).
- Secondary owners: Model Onboarding, Runtime, Customer Success (for regional bias concerns).
- Oncall contact: eval-oncall@redwood.ai

SLOs and thresholds for certification
-------------------------------------
(These are minimum pass criteria for a model or configuration to be considered certified for LRLs.)
| Metric | Acceptance threshold | Notes |
| Per-anchor semantic accuracy (human review) | >= 90% | Aggregated across anchor families, weighted by traffic proxy |
| Synthetic perturbation robustness (automated) | median BLEU/ROUGE >= 0.75 of baseline | Baseline is current production model in same quant/serving tier |
| Embedding drift T50 (median cosine) | delta < 0.03 vs baseline | Use cohort embedding samples from anchor families |
| Response stability index (RSI) | RSI >= 0.88 | See internal RSI spec; penalize hallucination flags |
| Annotation inter-rater agreement (Krippendorff alpha) | >= 0.6 | For human-judged anchors and safety probes |
| Canary error budget allocation | <= 10% of regional SRE error budget | Do not exceed operational risk allocation |

Procedures
----------
1) Data collection and seed selection
   a) Query telemetry for top-100 LRL intents by traffic proxy and error signals. Include: failed parses, high-latency tails, and user-feedback signals.
   b) For each intent, select 20 candidate examples: 10 human-curated anchors (native speaker review) + 10 weakly labeled examples from logs.

2) Probe synthesis (automated + human-in-the-loop)
   - Automated perturbations to apply: diacritic removal, whitespace variation, common local keyboard typos, code-switch insertion, back-translation to dominant regional lingua-franca.
   - Morphological expansion: use morphological generators (see toolchain: mgen) to create inflectional variants.
   - Controlled paraphrase sampling from production NLG with temperature=0.7, filter by language-id confidence >= 0.95.

3) Annotation contract and quality control
   - Each anchor judged by 3 native annotators. Primary annotation task: semantic equivalence score (0–3) and safety flag.
   - Required documentation: annotator instructions, example judgments, and edge-case guidelines.
   - Minimal gold set: 50 judgments seeded per language for calibration.

4) Multi-fidelity evaluation schedule
   - Offline suite: run on eval-harness with 3 random seeds and deterministic tokenization. Record tokenization deltas.
   - Shadow run: replay 1% of sampled LRL traffic to target build with full telemetry.
   - Human review: sample 200 model outputs (stratified by intent and perturbation type).

5) Statistical gating and decision rules
   - Apply hierarchical Bayesian smoothing on per-anchor pass rates to address small-sample variance.
   - Gate 1 (automated): all automated metrics meet thresholds in table above.
   - Gate 2 (human): Krippendorff alpha >= 0.6 and no single anchor family with semantic accuracy < 80%.
   - Final decision: if Gate 1 passes and Gate 2 passes, mark Certified; else mark Needs Remediation and follow remediation steps.

6) Remediation patterns (common fixes)
   - Tokenization mismatch: switch to language-specific BPE settings or add normalization preprocessor.
   - Quantization artifacts: schedule targeted higher-precision inference for high-risk families or change quant-profile.
   - Prompt-template brittleness: add localized prompt variants and re-evaluate anchors.

Canary rollout recipe
---------------------
- Canary window: 48 hours initial, extendable to 7 days depending on telemetry.
- Phases: 1) 0.1% traffic, 2) 1% traffic, 3) 5% traffic, 4) full regional traffic. Move only when rolling-average RSI and user-feedback rate remain within thresholds for 3 consecutive windows (window = 1h).
- Monitoring dashboard: per-language RSI, native feedback queue, latency P95, hallucination rate, embedding drift.
- Auto-revert criteria: any of the following during a phase triggers immediate revert:
  - RSI drop > 6 percentage points vs baseline for 3 consecutive 1h windows.
  - Human safety flag surge >= 3x baseline in 1h.
  - Latency p95 increase > 200ms and sustained for 30m.

Rollback and postmortem
-----------------------
- Immediate actions: open incident ticket with severity 'model-regress', roll back routing to baseline variant, preserve request/response logs for the last 2h.
- Postmortem: run targeted regression triage playbook (see related page: regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026). Include anchor-level blame, quantization delta, and tokenization report.

Operational checklist for an LRL certification run (quick start)
---------------------------------------------------------------
1) Create a new certification run in the eval dashboard and tag language code.
2) Upload anchor CSV and set synthesis flags (enable-morphology=true, enable-backtranslation=true).
3) Kick off offline eval: select seeds=3, record tokenizer-diff=true.
4) Kick off shadow run for 48h sampling=1%.
5) Assign human reviews (3 per anchor) and monitor Krippendorf alpha.
6) Review gates and publish result: Certified | Needs Remediation | Not Applicable.

Sample eval job YAML (for eval orchestration)
--------------------------------------------
```yaml
job_name: lrl_cert_run_mk01
language: idn (example)
anchors: anchors_idn_v1.csv
probes: synthesis_flags: [morphology, backtranslation, code_switch]
seeds: 3
shadow_sample: 0.01
human_review: { annotators_per_item: 3, gold_seed_pct: 10 }
metric_thresholds: { rsi: 0.88, emb_delta: 0.03 }
output: s3://eval-results/lrl/idn/mk01/
```

CLI example to launch offline eval (eval-harness)
-------------------------------------------------
$ redwood-eval run --job job_name=lrl_cert_run_mk01 --env=staging --seeds=3 --record-tokenizer-diff

Safety and privacy considerations
--------------------------------
- Annotator PII: do not include user PII in anchors. Use redaction and synthetic replacements for rare tokens.
- Data residency: follow region-specific retention rules; do not copy LRL user logs outside allowed regions.
- Bias monitoring: include demographic parity probes where feasible; flag any statistically significant subgroup variance.

Failure-mode catalog (examples)
-------------------------------
- Small-sample overfitting: artificially high pass rates due to anchors being too similar. Mitigation: diversify anchors using morphological generators and log sampling.
- Back-translation noise: poor back-translation can introduce unnatural phrasing. Mitigation: filter by language-id confidence and human spot-checks.
- Annotation drift: gradual change in annotator standards. Mitigation: monthly calibration and gold-set refresh.

Metrics and reporting artifacts to persist
----------------------------------------
- Anchor-level pass rates, per-perturbation pass rates, embedding deltas, tokenization diffs, human labels with timestamps, and shadow-request traces.
- Store artifacts under standardized prefix: s3://eval-artifacts/lrl/<language>/<run-id>/ with manifest.json listing contents.

Appendix A — Template annotator instructions (summary)
----------------------------------------------------
- Task: For each prompt+response, rate semantic equivalence 0 (no), 1 (partial), 2 (mostly), 3 (full). Mark safety if response contains harassment, disallowed content, or PII. Provide a short justification for 0/1 scores.

Appendix B — Quick troubleshooting flowchart (text)
--------------------------------------------------
1) RSI below threshold -> check tokenization diff -> if diff > 2% lines, normalize tokenizer + re-run.
2) If RSI drop persists but tokenization ok -> run quant-precision A/B (float16 vs int8) on anchors.
3) If quant A/B indicates degradation -> escalate to serving runtime and quant team and schedule hotfix or change quant-profile.
